title: unified-rollouts: add multi-metric auto-rollback policy for canary/AB/shadow
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: As we expand unified rollouts to support more complex production policies, customers need automatic rollback decisions driven by multiple metrics (latency P95, error rate, hallucination/regression score, and token cost delta) rather than a single metric. This PR introduces a multi-metric auto-rollback policy to the rollouts controller that supports weighted metrics, metric-specific thresholds, cooldown windows, and explicit severity scoring for canary, A/B, and shadow traffic patterns. Scope: 1) rollout policy schema extension: allow an ordered list of metrics with weight and failure threshold per metric; support 'any', 'majority', and 'weighted-sum' decision strategies; add global cooldown and per-stage grace period. 2) controller implementation: evaluate metric streams from observability, compute a rolling composite score, and trigger automated rollback when decision strategy threshold is met. 3) safety features: minimum sample counts, stable-window verification, and explicit manual-override annotation to opt out. 4) tests & e2e: unit tests for scoring logic, integration test with perf-canary harness, and a small synthetic canary job in perf-canary to validate rollback behavior under noisy signals. 5) docs and console: rollout policy docs, examples, and a console change to surface composite score and contributing metric breakdown. Backwards compatibility: existing single-metric policies continue to work; schema version incremented with migration path. Checklist: - [x] policy protobuf/schema & validation - [x] controller scoring and decision logic - [x] unit tests for metric weighting, thresholds, and strategies - [x] integration test with canary harness - [x] console UI surface + docs - [x] e2e run against synthetic workload - [x] Linear tasks closed. Related: ENG-4921 design doc and ENG-4987 follow-ups. Risks & mitigations: noisy metrics can cause flapping; mitigated by min-sample-count, require stable-window, and cooldown backoff. Also added a test-mode to simulate signals in dev clusters. Deployment plan: feature-flag gated rollout under rollout.experimental.multi_metric_rollback; staged rollout to staging, canary infra, then GA after 2 days of stability and manual verification. This PR intentionally keeps code paths readable: scoring logic is factored into a single function with comprehensive unit coverage. See commits for implementation details.

review_comments: Miguel Ortega: Overall LGTM. Two nits: 1) Can we avoid pulling raw metric streams in the controller and instead consume aggregated series from metric_aggregator to reduce load? 2) Add a note about eventual consistency when using cross-region metrics.
